artworks.title: Picking Cotton
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Josephine Boardman Crane, 1957)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a green field of cotton plants with white blossoms. Three individuals are seen harvesting the cotton. They appear to be wearing skirts and bonnets and have dark skin, although their faces aren’t detailed. The background includes buildings on the left and green trees against a pale blue sky with hints of grey. The painting utilizes loose, visible brushstrokes. The color scheme is warm and natural, featuring shades of green, brown, and muted tones.

artworks.title: Nearing the Issue at the Cockpit
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, 1899)
artworks.description: This painting shows a group of men gathered closely together, leaning over a wooden railing with their hands resting on it. The men are dressed in various attire including top hats, bowler hats, and flat caps, with a range of semi-formal to casual clothing such as black suits, brown coats, and plain shirts. They are a diverse group, with skin tones ranging from pale to dark brown, some with mustaches or beards and other bare faced. They all appear to be focused intently on something that is just below us, some with slight smiles, others with wide eyes and raised brows. The background includes a wooden beam ceiling and a partially peeling plaster wall with a framed document labeled "RULES" partially visible near the upper right. On the upper left, the graying plaster appears to have cracked off, revealing red brick.

artworks.title: Self-Portrait
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)

artworks.title: Marly-le-Roi
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a street scene from a slightly elevated perspective. A tan dirt road stretches into the distance, lined with white houses on the left side. On the right side is a tall fence, and behind it the green tops of trees or bushes are visible. People in dark clothing walk along the street in the distance. Beyond them, taller trees are visible, with more buildings below them. The sky above is softly colored in hues of yellow, peach, and gray. The brushstrokes are loose and visible.

artworks.title: Telemachus and Calypso
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Bernice West Beyers, 1963)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a coastal scene with a large group of people with light skin dressed in draping fabric in shades of red, yellow, blue, and purple. In the bottom left corner, two men, one old and one young, stand in front of a dark, stormy sea, upon which a large ship is tilting dramatically to one side near large, rocky cliffs. The sky above the ship is full of dark clouds, with streaks of bright yellow surrounded by magenta breaking through the gray. The men face the right, and the young man has his hand outstretched towards a group of women in a grassy meadow dotted with small flowers. One woman at the front of the group faces the men, her arm outstretched towards them. Three women sit at her feet, and a group of five women cluster behind her, hugging one another tightly. On the right, four more women dance in a group, their arms upraised and knees bent. Behind the meadow are tall, olive-green trees.

artworks.title: Simon Pease
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, William A. Clark Fund and Anna E. Clark Fund, 1965)
artworks.description: The portrait depicts a man standing with one hand resting on a blue fabric covered table. He has a dignified posture, relaxed shoulders, and a calm facial expression. He has fair skin, a rounded face, grayish-white hair styled in curls typical of the 18th century. The man is dressed in a dark coat with decorative buttons and wide-cuffed sleeves showing white ruffled cuffs. He wears a white cravat. The background includes a stone column and a view of a landscape with a blue sky, hills, clouds, and trees.

artworks.title: Negro Boys on the Quayside
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund and William A. Clark Fund, 1960)
artworks.description: The painting depicts four boys, sitting or leaning against boxes, a wooden platform, and a stone wall. The boy on the left is sitting on the wooden platform, leaning back with his legs crossed, and wearing a blue shirt, brown pants, and a wide-brimmed hat. Next to him, standing on the same platform and sitting on stacked boxes, are two of the other boys. One of these boys is wearing light-colored trousers and a buttoned-up vest underneath a light-colored jacket. The other boy stands slightly behind him, dressed in a red shirt, a dark vest, and a dark jacket, with a brown hat. The last boy, standing to the right and leaning against a low stone wall, is wearing dark-blue trousers, a brown jacket, and a wide-brimmed straw hat. All of the boys have brown skin and short, dark hair. The background showcases a bustling harbor scene with numerous docked sailing ships, buildings, and equipment, all under a pale gray sky.

artworks.title: Study for "Breton Women at a Pardon"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: Charles Sheeler and Nina Allender
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Joan B. Detweiler, 1962)

artworks.title: A Landscape after Sunset
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, William A. Clark Fund, Gallery Fund, and gifts of Orme Wilson, George E. Hamilton, Jr., and R. M. Kauffmann, 1963)
artworks.description: Three cows drink in a placid body of water in front of a landscape dim with golden sunset light in this horizontal painting. The water creates white eddies around a few rocks as it travels from the lower left corner of the canvas, across the foreground, and off to the right. In the bottom right quadrant of the composition, one cow is white, and another dark brown. The third, tawny brown cow flicks her tail as she dips her head to the water. Tall groves of trees on the far side of the water fill most of the right half of the composition. To the left, a path curves from the waterside back into a grassy, tree-pocked landscape with buildings on one low hill and a very distant horizon, which comes halfway up this composition. A person wearing a red vest over a white long-sleeved shirt, dark blue, knee-length pants, and a brown, brimmed hat rides a white horse coming toward us on the path. A short-hair, pale gray dog runs ahead of the horse, toward the cows. From below the horizon, the sunlight sets the grassy fields to golden tan, and the sky above fades from buttery yellow along the horizon to pale blue along the top of the composition. Lines of clouds are lit mauve pink and shaded ultramarine blue.

artworks.title: Cupid, Stung by a Bee, Is Cherished by his Mother
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Bernice West Beyers, 1963)
artworks.description: A seated woman wrapped in a spruce-blue garment embraces a tearful, winged boy in this round painting. Both have smooth, pale skin with flushed cheeks, delicate features, and golden-brown hair. The woman takes up most of the painting. She sits angled to our left as she curls both arms around the nearly nude boy, Cupid. Her hair is plaited at the back of her head behind a blue-green headband. The upper arm we can see is encircled with a gold band set with blue gems, and one breast is bare in the shadow over her crooked elbow. The other hand holds the boy’s middle finger. Cupid’s body faces our right, toward the woman, but he turns back to look at the hand the woman holds. His other hand is lifted to his eyes, and a tear gleams on one cheek. His body is covered only by a white cloth that crosses his chest and covers his genitals. A silvery-white and tawny-gold wing juts out behind one shoulder. The woman sits on a pillowy rust-red cushion. One gray dove feeds another at Cupid’s feet, and a pink rose lies nearby. A field of olive green and mustard yellow suggests a tree behind Cupid and the woman. In the distance to our left, three pale-skinned, chubby babies tussle with mouths wide open in a garden near a beehive. Bees teem out of the conical hive. Peach-colored clouds skim the muted blue sky above. The artist signed and dated the lower left, “B. West 1774.”

artworks.title: Landscape
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: Moonlight
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This painting shows a slightly elevated viewpoint looking out across a green landscape towards a reflective body of water. In the green sky, the pale-yellow moon glows brightly, illuminating the scene. At the top of the painting, greenish-yellow clouds with thin brown edges float across the sky. The moonlight reflects off the water, creating a bright pathway at the bottom of the painting. There are the dark silhouettes of trees on the left side, and in the distance the flat green landscape fades into the glowing atmosphere. The colors include muted greens, browns, and golds.

artworks.title: Mercy's Dream
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting an angel crowning a seated woman in a dark landscape. The angel has white wings with hints of pink and green, pale skin, and short, golden hair. They are draped in a flowing white robe, and have one hand extended upward and the other placing a golden crown on the woman's head. The woman sits below the angel, near the bottom left corner of the painting. Her eyes are closed, and she has one hand placed on her chest. She also has pale skin and golden hair, and she wears a draping white garment that hangs loosely off of her shoulders and is tied at the waist with what looks like white rope. Over her legs there appears to be a blanket in shades of coral pink and golden yellow. The background is dark, but seems to be a rocky terrain with sparse green grass and trees, under a dark sky with dramatic purple clouds and a hint of pink light emerging behind some rocky mountains on the right. The angel and woman are brightly illuminated against the dark background.

artworks.title: Sarah Shippen Lea (Mrs. Thomas Lea)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Anonymous gift, 1979)

artworks.title: A Celebration
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1891)
artworks.description: This is a painting of an interior scene featuring a group of finely dressed individuals in a lavish room. The room is adorned with red drapery, wooden paneling, and a tiled floor. There is a table set with glassware and a golden bowl. In the background, elegantly dressed figures, likely women in elaborate gowns, are seen standing and appearing to partake in a musical or theatrical performance, with musical instruments visible among them. The lighting is soft and warm, casting a gentle glow over the scene and emphasizing the textures and details of their clothing. This painting is in the style of Jean-Antoine Watteau.

artworks.title: Tourn Mountain, Head Quarters of Washington, Rockland Co., New York
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
artworks.description: A river winds from close to us to a distant mountain outlined against a dim sky in this horizontal landscape painting, which has a shallowly arched top. The rippling river bends from the bottom right corner of the canvas into the middle of the painting and then curves out of view in a grassy field. Wisps of fog to the right show the distant path of the river. Land in the lower left corner of the painting is loosely painted with earthy green and brown, which could represent grass, rocks, and fallen tree trunks. Sunlight warms a single-story, compact, white-walled house with a brown roof and a chimney in a clearing to the left. A few trees stand near the house, and a tree-carpeted mountain rises sharply beyond it. The mountain is backlit or thrown into shadow by the low sun. In the top quarter of the composition, pale peach-colored clouds kick up around the mountain against a pink-tinged horizon in the blue sky. The artist signed and dated the painting as if he had written on a rock in the lower center of the composition, “1851 J.F. Cropsey.”

artworks.title: Arsène Carriere
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
artworks.description: This image shows a young baby from head to toe. The baby is upright, possibly seated or reclined, with soft, rounded features, rosy cheeks, small eyes, and a slight smile. The hair is sparse and light-colored. The baby is dressed in a light-colored garment with red accents on the feet, likely the tops of booties or socks. The baby is holding a silver object attached to a ribbon or string in one hand, possibly a rattle. The background is dark with some red tones, offering a contrast with the light clothing. The artist's name, "Eugène Carrière," is visible in the upper left corner as a signature.

artworks.title: Conviviality Near the Inn
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This is a painting of an outdoor scene with numerous people engaged in various activities; some are sitting by low tables, some are dancing, and some are conversing. One person on the right stands on a surface and plays a stringed instrument like a fiddle or violin. The people wear clothes in earth shades of brown, tan, black, and dark red. The background includes a rustic building with a thatched roof, leafy green trees, and what may be a tall castle or church on the left. The cloudy sky above is in shades of gray.

artworks.title: Return from the Hunt
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: Thomas Jefferson
artworks.artist: George Peter Alexander Healy, after Gilbert Stuart
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, 1879)
artworks.description: This painting is a portrait of a seated man, seen from the waist up. The man's torso is turned slightly to the left, with his head turned to look at us. He has pale skin with high cheekbones, straight eyebrows, and thin lips set in a neutral expression. His hair is gray and appears to be tied in a low ponytail behind his head, with some curls around his ears. He is wearing a dark coat over a white shirt with a high collar. The background is blur of brown, and the chair he sits on is dark red.

artworks.title: Man with a Sheet of Music
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: Shown from the waist up, a bearded man with pale, peachy skin, wearing a black wide-brimmed hat and jacket, and a broad, layered, white collar, holds up a piece of rolled up paper in this vertical portrait painting. His shoulders are angled to our right but he turns his face to look at us with dark gray eyes. He has a bumped nose, and his full pink lips are slightly parted. There are bags under his heavy-lidded eyes. A light brown mole marks his soft cheek, on our left, and there are jowls along his jawline. His honey-brown goatee is trimmed to a point, and his brown curly hair falls to his collar. The wide brim of the hat sweeps down a bit to our right. Layers of white fabric create a wide collar that rests against his chest and nearly reaches his shoulders. His dark coat is a field of black, broken only by the sheer white cuff and the hand he holds up in front of his chest. The skin of that hand, his left, has a greenish cast, and he wears a gold ring on the pinky finger. Musical notation is visible on the rolled-up paper he holds loosely in that hand. He is lit from our upper left so casts a shadow against the peanut-brown wall behind him. The artist signed and dated the painting near the man’s shoulder, to our right: “Rembrandt f 1633.”

artworks.title: The Umbrian Mountains
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, William A. Clark Fund, 1928)

artworks.title: Seated Nude
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of A.M. and Lillian Adler, 1967)
artworks.description: This painting shows a woman sitting on a blue cushion with one leg bent and the other stretched out. She has dark hair styled in an updo and adorned with a hat or patterned headscarf that features small orange dots. Her facial features are blurred, slowing only dark eyes and a red mouth. She is nude, and her skin is cream-colored, with light pink areas on her face, neck, and chest. Her left hand is on the cushion beside her, while her right hand holds a small oval object up to her face. The background behind her is filled with abstract shapes in shades of blue, brown, gray and green, with hints of dark yellow and bright red. The brushstrokes in the painting are thick and visible, giving the scene a blurred appearance.
